title: Situated_approach_(artificial_intelligence)
summary:
In artificial intelligence research, the situated approach builds agents that are designed to behave effectively and successfully in their environment. This requires designing AI from the bottom up by focusing on the basic perceptual and motor skills required to survive. The situated approach gives a much lower priority to abstract reasoning or problem-solving skills.

The approach was originally proposed as an alternative to traditional approaches popular before 1985 or so. After several decades, classical AI technologies started to face intractable issues such as combinatorial explosion when confronted with real-world modeling problems. All approaches to address these issues focus on modeling intelligences situated in an environment and have become known as the situated approach to AI. During the late 1980s, the approach now known as Nouvelle AI was pioneered at the MIT Artificial Intelligence Laboratory by Rodney Brooks.

The main characteristics are that it is bottom-up, relying on elementary behaviors which can be combined to implement more complex behaviors, and it is behavior-based, not relying on a symbolic description of the environment but rather on a model of the interactions of entities with their environment. The goal of situated AI is to model entities that are autonomous in their environment, achieved through both the intrinsic robustness of the control architecture and its adaptation capabilities to unforeseen situations.

The most important attribute of a system driven by situated AI is that the intelligence is controlled by a set of independent semi-autonomous modules. This approach stems from early insights of Alan Turing, who described the need to build machines equipped with sense organs to learn directly from the real world instead of focusing on abstract activities such as playing chess. The vast majority of traditional technologies are based on the symbolic AI approach, which is top-down and knowledge-based, but the limits of traditional AI are well-known as a combinatorial explosion of rules occurs due to the complexity of the environment.
